directAnswer: To record your screen on Android, use the built-in screen recorder feature available in Android 10 and later, or download a third-party app if your device doesn't support it.
summary: Screen recording on Android devices can be done natively or through third-party applications, depending on your Android version.

sections.heading: Using the Native Screen Recorder
sections.body: Most Android devices running Android 10 or newer come with a built-in screen recording feature accessible through the Quick Settings menu.

sections.heading: Using Third-Party Apps
sections.body: If your device does not support native screen recording, consider using apps like AZ Screen Recorder or Mobizen, which offer additional features.

steps.title: Access Quick Settings
steps.detail: Swipe down from the top of your screen to open the Quick Settings menu.

steps.title: Start Screen Recording
steps.detail: Look for the 'Screen Record' icon. Tap it and select your recording preferences.

steps.title: Stop Recording
steps.detail: To stop recording, swipe down again and tap the 'Stop' button in the notification.

steps.title: Using a Third-Party App
steps.detail: Download a screen recording app from the Google Play Store, open it, and follow the app's instructions to start recording.

faqs.question: Can I record internal audio while screen recording?
faqs.answer: Some devices allow recording internal audio, but this feature may not be available on all devices or apps.

faqs.question: How long can I record my screen?
faqs.answer: The duration of screen recordings may vary by device and app, but typically you can record until your storage runs out.

faqs.question: Is there a limit to the number of recordings I can make?
faqs.answer: There is no inherent limit, but storage space on your device will determine how many recordings you can save.

caveats: Screen recording features may vary by device manufacturer and Android version.
